newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil drifts off gains, ends barely higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil drifts off gains, ends barely higher.

text.p: IPE gas oil retraced most of the day's gains to close barely above the opening in a lame consolidation on Thursday after two days of falls driven by bearish stock data and Iraq news, traders said.
Traders were slightly bearish on gas oil's outlook due partly to technical factors and partly to flat prompt physical demand.
January closed 25 cents higher at $205.25 a tonne, down $4 from the day's highs and $1 from mid-afternoon. December gas oil expired at $207.00 a tonne, down $4 from the highs.
January Brent was trading 27 cents higher at $21.91 a barrel, down from $22.46 in mid-afternoon and $22.60 at midday, having shed $1.14 in Wednesday's session.

"The gas oil came off a long way in a short space of time," said one trader. "It's really going through a consoldation but overall I'm a little bit negative. There's a good chance that the prompt gas oil could down through the 200 level."
Another trader said: "People are still a little apprehensive after what happened."
In NYMEX trade, January crude was 19 cents higher at $23.57, while Jan heat was 1.18 cents up at 68.00 cents.

Traders said the first Iraqi oil sales in six years, mild weather in the key heating oil market of the northeast United States and builds in U.S. oil stocks, remained as potential pressure points both gas oil and Brent futures.
American Petroleum Institute data released on Tuesday showed a 1.0 million barrel build nationwide, including a 665,000 barrel gain the northeast.
Physical delivery against the expired IPE December gas oil futures contract will be 879 lots, or 87,900 tonnes, an IPE official said. -- William Maclean, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7646x
